Grace / team — quick sizing sketch below (ballpark, for customer-facing pilot):

Assumptions:
- Avg request size: 1.2k tokens (prompt + response)
- Avg tokens/sec per A100-80GB (int8 optimized): 60 TPS for our model family at 512-beam parallelism
- Warm pool latency SLO: p95 <= 180ms

Sizing math (target 12k qps peak):
- Baseline sustained qps (p50 in their csv): ~2.5k qps => -> ~42 A100-equivalent slots (2.5k / 60)
- Peak 12k qps transient -> 200 A100-eq if fully cold (12k / 60)
- Warm pool strategy: maintain 30% warm pool of peak (60 A100-eq) to cover majority of spikes; autoscale add-to 200 with burst buffer and admission control.
- Recommended committed (reserved) for pilot: 70 A100-eq (covers baseline + warm pool cushion).
- Burst capacity via shared burstable nodes (preemptible) with autoscale to 200 for short windows; throttle admission for tail-preserving routing (detailed below).

Routing / fallback policy:
1) Route to primary private farm while probe detects warm pool health.
2) On warm pool depletion (queue depth > X or p95 latency > target), redirect low-priority traffic to hosted fallback model (lower-cost smaller model), preserve critical queries to private with admission control.
3) Use prefix caching for repeated prompts; cache hit ratio can cut token work by ~18% in our benchmarks.

Network egress rough numbers (very rough):
- Baseline outbound bandwidth: ~350 Mbps per 1000 qps (depends on payload size) -> for peak 12k qps ~4.2 Gbps.
- Recommend provisioning 10 Gbps per AZ for headroom and cross-AZ failover.

I'll draft the one-pager with these numbers. Happy to refine with Laura for network details and Rishi for SLA wording.

Adding network specifics and failure modes:

Network assumptions + mitigations:
- Payload estimate: 3.5 KB request + 7 KB response average => ~10.5 KB/req. At 12k rps = ~126 MB/s = ~1.0 Gbps (after overhead). Jonas' calc is conservative — tokenization influences but payload is prime driver.
- Cross-AZ replication: keep stateful caches local to AZ; replicate KV asynchronously for best-effort consistency to avoid cross-AZ tail-latency amplification.
- Egress budget: recommend at least 5 Gbps headroom per AZ for telemetry, prefetch, model downloads during rollouts. 10 Gbps is safe if customer expects growth beyond pilot.
- NAT/Gateway saturation: use multiple egress NAT instances per AZ, health-checked and with scaling policies. Monitor SNAT exhaustion (we've seen issues at ~30k concurrent sockets).

Warm pool & cache warmup:
- Warm pool target: 25–35% of peak (agrees with Jonas). Warm-start sequence: pre-populate KV caches + prefix cache + micro-batching ramp over 60–120s window to avoid stampeding.

Failure modes to call out in the one-pager:
1) Cross-AZ network partition: degrade to single-AZ active with admission control; broadcast degraded mode to customer UI (short notice).
2) Egress NAT exhaustion: route outgoing telemetry to secondary path; degrade non-critical telemetry.
3) Warm pool depletion -> fall through to hosted-lite model for non-critical queries.

Couple of additions on SLA and autoscale policing: 

SLA framing for pilot:
- Offer latency SLO classes: Critical (p95 <= 200ms), Best-effort (p95 <= 500ms). Tie routing policy to SLO class.
- Escape hatch: explicit fallback window (e.g., 2–5 minutes) where we run aggressive admission control before failing queries; log and expose metrics to Acme's dashboard.

Autoscale rules: 
- Pre-scale window: detect slope (delta qps / minute) > threshold -> pre-warm add N nodes proportional to slope to avoid cold-start penalty.
- Admission control: token-bucket per-tenant to avoid head-of-line blocking; drop or route to hosted-lite when queue > q_thresh.
- Billing / commercial: recommend reserved commit = baseline+warmpool (Jonas' 70 A100-eq). Burstable capacity billed at per-minute usage; include a runway credit if they commit 12+ months.

I'll help craft the SLA appendix and short redlines for procurement. I've attached draft_sla_redlines.pdf for internal review.
